extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (patent prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on shortened statutory periods, specified time limits, and procedures for obtaining extensions of time in U.S. patent prosecution (37 CFR 1.136 and related practice in the MPEP). Covers when and how extensions may be obtained, exceptions, fee treatment, and consequences of late or missing replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a) — Extensions up to five months with petition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed, unless: (i) Applicant is notified otherwise in an Office action; (ii) The reply is a reply brief under § 41.41; (iii) The reply is a request for an oral hearing under § 41.47(a); (iv) The reply is to a decision by the PTAB under § 41.50 or § 41.52 or to § 90.3; or (v) The application is involved in a contested case or a derivation proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for purposes of determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee. A reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment. In no situation may an applicant reply later than the maximum time period set by statute. Petition and fee may be filed with or without the reply; filing the petition and fee makes the extension effective upon filing without Office acknowledgement. See exceptions listed above and MPEP cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(b) — Extensions for sufficient cause when (a) unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply cannot be filed within the time period set and the provisions of paragraph (a) are not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Any request for an extension under this paragraph must be filed on or before the day on which such reply is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a request under (b) will not effect any extension. Extensions under (b) are to be decided by the Technology Center (TC) Director. No extension may carry the reply date beyond the maximum statutory period. Requests under (b) must state a reason (sufficient cause) and supply the fee. Use of form paragraphs is suggested for late replies when extension may be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) — Constructive petition by prior authorization or fee submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request may be submitted in an application that is an authorization to treat any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension of time as incorporating a petition for extension of time. An authorization to charge required fees or submission of the fee set forth in § 1.17(a) will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring such a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is a “safety net” to avoid loss of patent rights where a petitioner inadvertently omitted a petition. Office practice treats prior authorizations or fee submissions as constructive petitions for concurrent or future replies. The Office strongly recommends including a written petition with any desired extension in the reply to avoid processing delays. Examples and office practice (treating late two-month petitions as requesting three months if authorization present) are given in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-extendable periods following a Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, certain time periods are not extendable if set in the Notice of Allowability or in an Office action having a mail date on or after the mail date of the Notice of Allowability: (1) period for submitting the inventor’s oath or declaration; (2) period for submitting formal drawings set under § 1.85(c); (3) period for making a deposit set under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are not available to extend these particular periods if they are set in the Notice of Allowability or in Office actions mailed on/after its mail date. Be aware of this limitation when planning prosecution and fee submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum and common shortened statutory periods (35 U.S.C. 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period under authority of 35 U.S.C. 133 may not be less than 30 days. The Patent Law Treaty provides for at least two months for replies to most Office actions; the Office uses specific shortened periods depending on the type of reply required (examples include 2 months for restriction/election-only, inadvertent omission correction, Ex parte Quayle matters; 3 months to reply to any Office action on the merits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The length of the shortened statutory period depends on the type of reply required; specific situations enumerated in MPEP indicate when two-month or three-month periods are set. Some Office pilot programs may set periods shorter than two months. An indication of a shortened time for reply should appear prominently on the first page of actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits for particular actions (not shortened statutory periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may specify a time for applicant to take some action where failure results in a consequence other than abandonment. Specified time limits can be less than the 30-day statutory minimum and are used in situations such as: (A) petition under 37 CFR 1.14(a) for access — usually 3 weeks to state objections; (B) completion of an IDS where part omitted — 1-month time limit; (C) cancelling claims to nonelected invention or petitioning restriction — e.g., 2 months; (D) requiring an added claim to provoke an interference — period not less than one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely comply with a specified time limit generally will not result in abandonment but will have specific consequences (e.g., Office will decide petition without applicant input, noncomplying IDS information will be placed in file but not considered, cancellation treated as authorization). Specified time limits should be used where failure will not produce abandonment; if the failure could result in abandonment, a time period should be set that is not subject to extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction and consequences: shortened statutory periods vs specified time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified time limit differs from a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133: (A) failure to meet a specified time results in loss of rights only in regard to that particular matter, while failure to meet a shortened statutory period results in abandonment of the entire application; (B) specified time limits may be less than 30 days; (C) examiners may excuse small delays for specified times but not for shortened statutory periods (a day or two late in a shortened statutory period results in abandonment regardless of excuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the harsh consequence of missing shortened statutory periods (abandonment, only revivable by petition to revive if delay was unintentional). Some appeal-related periods (e.g., 2-month appeal brief filing) are time periods but not statutory periods under 35 U.S.C. 133 and therefore extendable under 1.136(a). Always note whether a period is identified as statutory for 35 U.S.C. 133 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restarting the reply period when Office action contains defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the citation of a reference is incorrect or an Office action contains some other defect and this error is called to the attention of the Office within 1 month of the mail date of the action, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must call the error to the Office within one month of mailing to obtain restart. See MPEP § 710.06 for details and required requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent notice requirement for shortened statutory periods/time limits on first page
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of a shortened time for reply should appear prominently on the first page of all copies of actions in which a shortened time for reply has been set so that a person merely scanning the action can easily see it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use capital letters where required. This is an examiner instruction so applicants scanning first page will be aware of shortened statutory periods or time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and fee treatment for extensions (fee amount determines extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is used to determine the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee. The expiration of the time period is determined by the amount of the fee paid. The fees for extensions under § 1.136(a) are set forth in § 1.17(a) and are cumulative; small entity and micro entity reductions apply (60% and 80% respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incremental extension is sought after paying a smaller fee (e.g., paid 1-month fee then later needs another month), the proper fee is the amount set forth for the longer extension less the amount previously paid. Applicants should ensure correct cumulative payment. Examples in the MPEP illustrate fee computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to availability of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions with payment of a fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not available in certain situations, including: (A) all extensions in a reexamination proceeding; (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding (but not preparatory to an interference where a claim is suggested); (C) situations where an Office action states 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to notice of allowability, reissue applications associated with litigation, or where nonelected claims/time set to cancel such claims); (D) limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference applicable CFR sections and MPEP chapters (ex parte reexamination, inter partes reexamination, interferences) to determine whether (a) is applicable. If (a) is not available, consider (b) or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice treating certain late petitions as requesting necessary extension when authorization present
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition for an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requests an insufficient period such that the petition would be filed outside the so-extended period for reply, but the period could be further extended under 1.136(a) so the petition would be filed within the further extended period, Office practice is to treat the petition as requesting the period necessary to make the petition filed within the further extended period if the petition or application contains an authorization to charge extension fees or fees under § 1.17 to a deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a two-month petition filed 4.5 months after a notice of appeal may be treated as requesting three months if authorization to charge fees is present. This practice applies even if no further reply is filed; constructive petitions under 1.136(a)(3) apply where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested short form petition language
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper petition may be only a few sentences such as: 'The applicant herewith petitions the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office to extend the time for reply to the Office action dated ____ for ____ month(s) from ____ to ____. Submitted herewith is a check for $____ to cover the cost of the extension [Please Charge my deposit account number ____, in the amount of $____ to cover the cost of the extension.]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office strongly recommends including a written petition with the reply to avoid processing delays. The sample includes options for check or deposit-account charge and suggests including instructions for charge/credit of deficiencies or overpayments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a reply after the set period without petition/fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period for reply has expired and no petition or fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be a constructive petition under 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted. If the fee is not filed until later months, additional fees for intervening months are required in order to render the reply timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: action sets a 3-month shortened statutory period, applicant replies in the 4th month and includes only a 1-month petition — reply is not acceptable until the proper fee (and possible additional fees for 2nd month) are filed. Ensure petition+appropriate fee are filed to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for first reply after final rejection and advisory action timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant initially replies within 2 months from the date of mailing of any final rejection (where a 3-month shortened statutory period is set) and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for purposes of determining the amount of any extension fee will be the date on which the Office mails the advisory action advising applicant of the status of the application, but in no event can the period extend beyond 6 months from the date of the final rejection. The following language must be included by the examiner in each final rejection: (text requiring the shortened statutory period to expire three months and conditions regarding advisory actions and the six-month maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner mails an advisory action before end of 3 months, shortened period expires at 3 months; if advisory action is mailed after 3 months, period expires on advisory action mailing date. In no event will statutory period expire later than six months from the final action mailing date. See MPEP § 706.07(f) for cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after final rejection — examiner discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants request an extension of time after final rejection to submit an affidavit, granting the request is without prejudice to the examiner’s right to question why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented. If applicant’s showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding the previous grant of an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide persuasive reasons for late affidavits; even if an extension is granted, entry of the affidavit remains within examiner discretion and may be denied if the showing is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for processing 1.136(b) duplicate requests and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension under 37 CFR 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate and accompanied by a stamped return-addressed envelope, the Office will indicate the action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly in the envelope. The notation on the original (which becomes part of the file) should be signed by the person granting or denying the extension and the returned copy should bear the name and title of that person. When granted in part or denied, the extent/reason will be clearly indicated on both original and returned copy or a formal decision letter will be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure is optional for applicant to request. Applicant should be advised promptly regarding action taken so that the file record will be complete. Use form paragraphs 7.98/7.98.01 where appropriate for late replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on hand-delivery of extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-carried requests for extensions of time will no longer be accepted in the Technology Centers (TCs). Hand-carried requests may only be delivered to the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 501 for procedures regarding hand-delivery of papers and required information.
